q1.sql:
-- New customers and spend by channel, August 2026
select
    channel,
    signup_month,
    new_customers,
    spend
from marts.acquisition_by_channel
where signup_month between '2026-08-01' and '2026-08-31'

q2.sql:
-- Site sessions over the last 30 days
select
    count(session_id) as sessions
from marts.web_sessions
where session_date >= dateadd('day', -30, current_date)

t1.given: A CSV of Q3 cost-per-customer targets by channel, shared by the builder

v1.sql:
-- August new customers, spend and cost per new customer by channel
select
    channel,
    new_customers,
    spend,
    spend / new_customers as cost_per_customer
from q1
order by cost_per_customer desc
v1.notes: Spend is media spend only, excludes agency fees.

v2.sql: SELECT c.channel, c.cost_per_customer FROM v1 c ORDER BY 2 DESC

v3.sql:
-- Paid channels only
select
    channel,
    cost_per_customer
from v2
where channel in ('paid_search', 'paid_social')

f1.sql:
select cost_per_customer
from v1
where channel = 'paid_search'
f1.label: Paid search cost per new customer, August

f2.sql:
select target_cost_per_customer
from t1
where channel = 'paid_search'

f3.label: Paid search cost over target, August

i1.text: Paid search cost $61.20 per new customer in August, 11.3% over the $55.00 target.

i2.text: Industry benchmarks put paid search cost per customer around $50.

i3.text: Creative fatigue on the summer campaign is the likely driver.

i4.text: Costs should ease in September once the new creative is live.
